title: Mixed Feelings, Overall Satisfied for My Use
text:
Mixed Feelings, Overall Satisfied for My Use. I have some mixed feelings about the NOXU White L Shaped Desk with Shelves. I assembled this myself, but for those that get overwhelmed easily with boxed furniture assembly, you may need a buddy to assist. I've assembled another desk that was also L-shaped of the same price range. In comparison, this one isn't as sturdy and the assembly was complicated. I've assembled many pieces of boxed furniture, and this isn't the worst piece to assemble, but much more complicated than it should be as there are no moving parts. Not all of the pieces were labeled, and some of the written instructions didn't match up to the diagrams. The instructions are in need of revision. When I was in doubt, I referenced the diagrams. Some of the bolt alignments that attach the frame to the desktop were misaligned. This isn't something I've observed in the desks I have assembled in the past. This took me about 30 - 40 minutes of assembly time using an electric screwdriver. I strongly suggest to avoid tightening all the bolts/screws completely until you have an entire section aligned for the best fit. Small tools are included, but I only used the wrench as I prefer my own screwdriver over the small one that was included. It's not something I would consider incredibly sturdy. There could be some engineering improvements to the frame at the point of the back corner assembly, which would make it much more sturdy. The corner section is the weakest point, and the section over the shelves is the strongest point. Two points of attachment for the foot rest would also lend to a more sturdy design. As it's designed, I do not consider the foot rest sturdy.

The desktop is thin as is the metal of the hollow tubes that make up the frame. On the upside, it's light-weight for the size. I'm using it in my hobby room where I do small crafting projects and sewing. This desk replaced two older mis-matched desks I was using before. It does make for an aesthetic improvement. For my purpose, it's a good fit for my space and works well enough. I was mostly attracted by the shape and white color that better coordinates with my shelving units. The shelves are handy to have, and do add some stability. The feet on the desk are adjustable, so with some fine-tuning, you should be able to make it level on most floors. The computer stand will only work well on a carpeted surface as it's a slide design (no wheels) and not attached to the desk. I had a couple pieces of the frame arrive warped, with no damage to the packaging. This is a quality control issue. It was still able to be assembled, but I have a tapered gap between one of the rectangle parts and the corner piece. It's not a deal-breaker, but looks a bit sloppy. I would not attempt to bend it back into the right shape without risking the integrity of a welded seam. There is also some paint that was scratched on the frame, not due to the packaging, another quality control issue. If I had not received this desk in exchange for a review, I would attempt to return it for another.

If it were not for the quality control issues, I would consider this a very fair value. However, based on my personal experience, I cannot strongly recommend this particular desk based on quality control and needed improvements to the frame engineering. On the same note, if this desk fits your ideal dimensions for your space, and you do not intend to use it for anything that would need to withstand a heavy weight, it is not anything I would strongly discourage. For the size, it is a budget-friendly desk, but keep in mind it's budget quality as well. I hope you find my personal experience helpful, and kindly will click the button below.
